# B611 — Every `[derive(..)]` over a struct (or enum) with a `<const N>` parameter fails: "in code generated by this attribute: `N` is a length parameter: give it a number or another length parameter, not the type `N`" - macro_std's `GenericParameter` carries no const flag, so `binders` spells `type N`

- status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-11 (debug-50's find, Order 50)
- kind: bug (macro surface; S–M)
- area: Macros & derives

`[derive(PartialEq)] struct Buf<T, const N> { items: [T; N] }` (and Debug, Json, Default, Hashable alike) is refused inside the generated impl, because `derive_binders` (macro_std meta.vl) renders every generic as `type X[: Trait]` and the compiler's reflection of the generics does not say a parameter is a length. Fix: add `is_const: bool` to `GenericParameter` (the analyzer builds it at expansion time) and render `const N` in `derive_binders` and the bare name in `subject_spelling`; then pin one derive per trait over a `Buf<T, const N>`. Sizing S–M; lang-50 / the macro surface (not debug-50's files). Found probing E283's array half: a `[derive(Debug)]` over `[T; N]` is the natural use of the any-length impl.
